name: The Wreck-Shrines
summary: Shrines older than the Greenwood Compact, built into the hulls and bones of ships beached along the skeleton coasts. No living faith claims them; every crew that wrecks nearby leaves an offering anyway, and the Storm-Bound's tide-moots open with a circuit of the nearest shrine.

geography.character: beached hull-shrines on storm-coasts: rib-arches, figureheads as idols, tide-pool offering basins

notable_sites.name: The Keel-Mother
notable_sites.note: The largest shrine — an entire whale-ship set keel-up, its hold a chapel. Parley held within its shadow is sacred to every crew, Courts and Storm-Bound alike.

lore_notes: Wreck-shrine offerings are never taken; even the Skeleton Courts' Articles forbid it, and the Articles are enforced by people who enforce little else.
Their builders are unknown — pre-Compact stonework under post-Sundering hulls in some, which satisfies no chronology anyone has proposed.
adventure_hooks: An offering vanishes from three shrines in one tide; the crews assume it was outsiders and prepare to be right.
A wrecked crew washes ashore alive with no ship and no memory of water.
